findings.title: Fallback lookup crashes when SiteSetting/default locale is unavailable
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym on every fallback computation. Before the database/settings are ready (boot, rake tasks, migrations, asset precompilation, or a nil/blank default_locale) SiteSetting can raise or return nil, and nil.to_sym raises NoMethodError. Because the I18n fallbacks backend invokes this on translation lookups, a routine translation can crash boot or request handling instead of falling back to :en.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, and missed fallbacks get cached
findings.body: Fallback translations are loaded only by ApplicationController#set_locale calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Background jobs, mailers, console/rake code and other non-controller paths set I18n.locale without this call, and I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only loads config.locale. In those contexts a key missing from the primary locale will be looked up in fallback locales whose YAML was never loaded, return a missing-translation string, and for argument-less translations that result is frozen into the LRU cache keyed only by key+locale+backend, poisoning later web requests until reload.

findings.title: Translation cache ignores the dynamic fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU cache key is "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" but the resolved value now depends on FallbackLocaleList, i.e. on SiteSetting.default_locale at lookup time. If an admin changes the site default locale, or a translation is first resolved before its fallback locale is loaded, the cached value for the user locale remains stale/frozen and is served indefinitely (up to cache eviction/reload) instead of the translation from the new fallback locale.

findings.title: I18n.fallbacks is replaced with a Hash that does not implement the Fallbacks API
findings.body: I18n.fallbacks is assigned a plain Hash subclass whose [] always computes a new array and ignores stored entries. Code and gems expecting the I18n::Backend::Fallbacks object installed by Rails/i18n (e.g. assigning fallbacks per-locale with []=, reading defaults, or calling methods other than the newly added ensure_loaded!) will silently lose assignments or fail. In environments where Rails still sets config.i18n.fallbacks, Rails can also overwrite this object with a real Fallbacks instance that has no ensure_loaded!, making ApplicationController#set_locale raise NoMethodError.

findings.title: Every fallback lookup performs a SiteSetting lookup
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale on each invocation, and the fallbacks backend invokes [] for translation lookups (including repeated/missing keys). This adds a settings/cache lookup to hot I18n paths that the translate accelerator is specifically trying to keep fast, instead of computing and memoizing the chain per locale and invalidating it when the site locale changes.
